Disclosure to Promote the Right To Information 

Whereas the Parliament of India has set out to provide a practical regime of right to 
information for citizens to secure access to information under the control of public authorities, 
in order to promote transparency and accountability in the working of every public authority, 
and whereas the attached publication of the Bureau of Indian Standards is of particular interest 
to the public, particularly disadvantaged communities and those engaged in the pursuit of 
education and knowledge, the attached public safety standard is made available to promote the 
timely dissemination of this information in an accurate manner to the public.

0, FOREWORD 

0;l This Indian Standard was adopted by the 
Indian Standards Institution on 26 November 1973, 
after the draft finalized by the Cotton and Cotton 
Products Sectional Committee had been approved 
by the Textile Division Council. 

0.2 Poplin is generally defined as a fabric in which 
the end density is about twice the pick density and 
either the warp and weft counts are equal or the 
weft count is slighiiy coarser. The general range of 
construction of poplins is 90 ends to 150 ends with 
corresponding pick densities. TTie general weight 
per square metre of the fabric is between 85 and 150 
g/ml 

0.3 The breaking load values of poplins of super- 
fine, fine and medium varieties are under e^lua- 
tion and would be included in thestandard at a later 
stage. 

0.4 For the purpose of deciding whether a par- 
ticular requirement of this standard is a)mplied 
with, the final value, observed or calculated, ex- 
pressing the result of a test, shall be rounded off in 
accordance with IS 2 : 1^)*. The number of 
significant places retained in the rounded off value 
should be the same as that of the specified value in 
this standard. 



1, SCOPE 

1.1 This standard prescribes the requirements of 
market varieties of cotton poplin. 

1.2 This standard does not specify the shade, 
appearance and fee! of the cloth, 

2. REQUIREMENTS 

2,1 The requirements of poplin along with the 
relevant methods of tests are given in Table 1.

3. MARKING 

3.1 The cloth shall be marked with the following: 

a) Name of the material, namely, cotton poplin; 

b) Man ufacturer's name, initials or trade-mark; 

c) Month and year of manufacture; 

d) Dimensions of the piece; and 

e) Type of febr ic finish, such as bleached, dyed, 
preshrunk or mercerized. 

3.1.1 The cloth may also be marked with Standard 
Mark. 

3.1.2 The use of the Standard Mark is governed by 
the provisions of Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 
1986 and the Rules and Regulations made there- 
under. The details of conditions under which the 
licence for the use of Standard Mark may be granted 
lo manufacturers or producers may be obtained 
from the Bureau of Indian Standards. 

4. PACKING 

4.1 The cloth shall be packed in bales or cases in 
conformity with the procedure laid down either in 
IS 1347 : 1972* or in IS 293 : I967t, as agreed upon 
between the buyer and the seller. 

5. DECLARATION AND TOLERANCE 

5.1 The manufacturer shall declare the construc- 
tional particulars, namely, count of warp and weft 
yarn, number of ends and picks per decimetre and 
weight. 

5.2 The tolerances as given below shall be per- 
mitted on the constructional particulars : 

Count of warp and weft yarn 
Ends per dm and picks per dm 



Weight (g/m'^)

major flaws (see Appendix A) and shall be con- 
sidered as satisfactory If the number of serious and 
major Haws do not exceed the following limits: 



Serious flaws

7. SAMPIJNG 

7.1 For ascertaining the conformiiy in respect of 
length, width, breaking load, ends, picks, and 
weights, the procedure given in IS 3919 : ]966t shall 
be followed, 

7.2 For ascertaining the conformity in respect of 
visual defects at least 200 m of cloth from each bale 
selected according to 4 of IS 3919 : 1966t shall be 
inspected. The !ot shall be considered conforming 
in respect ofvisual defects if the requirementsgivcn 
in 6 are satisfied. 

7.3 For ascertaining the conformity in respect of 
shrinkage and colour fastness, the procedure given 
in IS 5463 : 1969i shall be followed.

7,4 For ascertaining the conformity in respect of 
'wash-and-wear' properties, the numbers of lest 
shall be equal to that for shrinkage. The lot shall be 
considered conforming to the requirements of 
'wash-and-wear' property if all the lest specimens 
satisfy the relevant requirements.

A-l SI'IRIOUS FLAWS 

4-1.1 One or more ends missing in the body of the 
material throughout its length, or more than three 
ends missing at a place and running over 60 cm or 
prominently noticeable double end running 
throughout the piece. 

A-1.2 Undressed snarls noticeable over a length 
exceeding 5 percent of the length of the piece.

A-2. MA.10RFI^WS 

A-2A Weft crack or two or more missing picks 
across the width of the fabric. 

A-2.2 Weft bar due to the difference in raw

A-2.3 More than two adjacent ends running 
parallel or broken or missing and extending beyond

the fabric.
